Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk...`
findings.fix: Remove role="status" unless this card's content is actually updated dynamically via JavaScript; if it is static, use a plain `<div>` or `<section>`.
findings.violation: role="status" marks an ARIA live region meant for dynamically-updating content announced automatically to assistive technology, but this div contains static, unchanging text, which is a misuse of the live-region role.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` preceded by "For the full list of upcoming adjustments,"
findings.fix: Change the link text to accurately describe the destination, e.g., "view fare adjustment history."
findings.violation: The link text says "accessibility improvements list" but the surrounding sentence is about "upcoming adjustments" (fare adjustments) and the href points to "/fares/history" - the link text does not describe its actual destination or purpose, which is misleading, especially for screen-reader users who navigate by link text.

findings.evidence: Label text "Phone number (required)" but the input is `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">` with no `required` or `aria-required` attribute
findings.fix: Add `required` (or `aria-required="true"`) to the phone input to match the label's stated requirement.
findings.location: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label"> and <input id="phone" type="tel" ...> in <form id="s3-form">
findings.violation: The label visually/textually indicates the field is required, but this isn't reflected in the markup, so assistive technology and form validation won't actually treat it as required.

findings.evidence: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded on page load, and the error span has no `aria-describedby` linking it to the input
findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid="false"` (or omit it) until actual validation fails, and add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the input.
findings.location: <input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true"> and <span class="error-text" aria-live="polite" id="s3-form-promo-error"> in <form id="s3-form">
findings.violation: Marking the field invalid before any user input is entered is incorrect and will cause screen readers to announce an error prematurely; additionally, the error text is not programmatically associated with the input via aria-describedby, so screen reader users may not hear why the field is invalid.

findings.evidence: None of the form controls have a `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes (e.g., name="email", name="phone", name="promo", name="topic") to each form control.
findings.location: <input id="email" ...>, <input id="phone" ...>, <input id="promo" ...>, and <select id="topic"> in <form id="s3-form">
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes, these fields won't be submitted with identifiable keys when the form is posted, breaking form submission.
